column3: “Settle” renders giving them rest on their land.
“Israel” and “the nations” supply the referents of the pronouns.
“Song of contempt” specifies the kind of saying.
“Your fate” supplies the object of their pondering.
“Dumped into a rocky pit” recasts going down to the stones of the pit.
“Owls” identifies the named animal differently from hedgehogs.
“Mountain” is singular where the Hebrew has mountains; “My people” supplies a pronoun’s referent, and shoulders are plural instead of singular.
The final active verb with an unspecified subject is rendered passively.
